# Frozen Contract v3.5 output contract

```text
<run-dir>/
├── grounding_receipt.json       # deterministic release/hash binding
├── grounding_view.json          # compact approved generation authority
├── run_manifest.json
├── learner_profile.json
├── adaptation_plan.json
├── adapted_content.md
├── provenance.json
├── code_validation.json
├── exercise_validation.json
├── validation_report.json
└── adaptation_summary.md
```

`prepare_frozen_grounding.py` must create the first two files before any generation. Do not copy or regenerate `source_manifest.json`, `core_invariants.json`, source claims, or the complete Frozen Contract inside the run directory.

`grounding_receipt.json` binds the run to the released Contract, Validator report, Release Gate report, inventory, source hashes, and reviewer record. `grounding_view.json` is a deterministic, token-efficient projection containing only approved canonical content. Never edit either file manually.

Every required Contract item in the view must appear in `adaptation_plan.json` and section provenance. Every conditional item must have exactly one include/exclude decision; included conditional items must also appear in plan and provenance. Excluded Contract items must never appear. Plan, content, and provenance must contain the same section IDs and headings in the same order.

`run_manifest.json.word_count_protocol` fixes the enabled state, inclusive limits, and `english_prose_v1` counting method. This method removes fenced code, HTML comments, displayed and inline math, and inline code before counting English word tokens. The final Validator records the count and fails the run when an enabled interval is missed.

When exercise generation is enabled, `run_manifest.json` fixes the count, required types, and solution policy. `adaptation_plan.json.exercise_section_id` identifies the final planned chapter, and every exercise and worked solution must appear there after all instructional content. Exercise IDs are consecutive in reading order. Every `exercise_plan` record must use selected lesson Contract items and have matching hidden content markers and exercise provenance. An objective-based update uses one `objective_gradient_update` record containing the objective, variables, point, step size, expected gradient, and expected update. Automatic differentiation supplies the gradient, and that same value supplies the update. Numeric exercises expose both `Result from the derivation` and `Checked answer` as JSON values and they must match the computed result and each other. Every Python block belonging to a code-verified exercise exposes a JSON-string `Expected output`, matched exactly against captured stdout. `exercise_validation.json` is generated by script and must not be hand-edited.

The student-facing lesson must not expose RC IDs. Exercise, solution, derived-answer, answer, and expected-stdout identifiers are hidden HTML comments; their result labels and values are visible. `validation_report.json` records `validation_scope=grounding_and_configured_checks_only` and verifies Frozen Contract binding, declared coverage, requested length, exercise structure, and configured automatic checks. It creates no post-generation human-review task and makes no complete-correctness claim.
